theory.intro: A ratio is in **simplest form** when its parts are whole numbers with no common factor except $1$. Divide **every** part by their highest common factor (HCF), just as you simplify a fraction. This gives an equivalent ratio, so the comparison is unchanged.
facts: $4:5$ is already in simplest form, because its only common factor is $1$.
Ratios with three parts simplify the same way — divide every part by the HCF of all three.
Dividing by a common factor that is not the highest leaves the ratio only partly simplified: $12:18=6:9$ still has a common factor of $3$.
steps: Check that measured quantities use the same units. If the units differ, convert all quantities to the smaller common unit to avoid decimals.
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of all the parts.
Divide every part by the HCF.
Check the new parts share no common factor other than $1$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Simplify $66:102$. Explain why $33:51$ is not fully simplified.
(b) Simplify $13:20$.
(c) Show that $55:85$ describes the same comparison as $66:102$.
(d) Simplify $\frac{66}{102}$. What is the same about the ratio and fraction methods?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The HCF of $66$ and $102$ is $6$.
$66:102=(66\div6):(102\div6)=11:17$
$33:51$ is equivalent, but both parts still share the factor $3$.
(b) The only common factor of $13$ and $20$ is $1$. The ratio $13:20$ is already in simplest form.
(c) The HCF of $55$ and $85$ is $5$.
$55:85=(55\div5):(85\div5)=11:17$
Both ratios have the same simplest form.
(d) $\frac{66}{102}=\frac{66\div6}{102\div6}=\frac{11}{17}$.
Both methods divide the two numbers by their HCF.

(a) Count $10$ shaded squares and $14$ unshaded squares.
Write shaded squares to unshaded squares.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}10:14\\&=(10\div2):(14\div2)\\&=5:7\end{aligned}$
Use the unshaded count, not the total number of squares.
(b) The rest of the class has $46-18=28$ students.
Write choir students to the rest of the class.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}18:28\\&=(18\div2):(28\div2)\\&=9:14\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: Mia simplifies $36\text{ mm}:9\text{ cm}$ to $4:1$. Explain her mistake and simplify the ratio correctly.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The quantities use different units. Convert centimetres to millimetres first: $9\text{ cm}=90\text{ mm}$.
The HCF of $36$ and $90$ is $18$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}36:90\\&=(36\div18):(90\div18)\\&=2:5\end{aligned}$
Both parts now use the same unit and share no common factor greater than $1$.

workedExamples.question_text: A ratio has simplest form $4:7$. Give one possible original ratio with both parts greater than $20$, and check it by simplifying.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply both parts by the same number, $6$.
$4:7=(4\times6):(7\times6)=24:42$
Both parts are greater than $20$. Their HCF is $6$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}24:42\\&=(24\div6):(42\div6)\\&=4:7\end{aligned}$

mastery.question_text:
Simplify $120:300$ and simplify $\frac{120}{300}$.
What is the same about the two methods?
mastery.solution_text:
$120:300=(120\div60):(300\div60)=2:5$
$\dfrac{120}{300}=\dfrac{120\div60}{300\div60}=\dfrac{2}{5}$
Both divide the two numbers by their HCF, $60$; a ratio and a fraction are simplified in exactly the same way.

mastery.question_text: Show that $16:24$ and $30:45$ describe the same comparison.
mastery.solution_text:
$16:24=(16\div8):(24\div8)=2:3$
$30:45=(30\div15):(45\div15)=2:3$
Both have simplest form $2:3$, so they describe the same comparison.
